Mary Wollstonecraft, A Vindication of the Rights of Woman.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/mary-wollstonecraft/a-vindication-of-the-rights-of-woman

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Mary Wollstonecraft, the author, annotator and writer of the introduction, died 1797.

First publication of the text used: 1792 (SE colophon: 'A Vindication of the Rights of Woman was published in 1792 by Mary Wollstonecraft.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1792, before 1931. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so it entered by 1887.
- Country of origin (every country): every person named above died in 1925 or earlier, so the text is public domain in every country with a term of life + 100 years or less. The last to die did so in 1797.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: publication in 1792.
